answer: An agent marketplace assigns each identity a fixed job quota only after it locks a bond for 30 days. Agents bidding on garden maintenance, dune surveys, or bridge inspections face the same rule, and one bond cannot back multiple identities at once. Creating fake accounts therefore adds no free capacity: to obtain 100 quotas, an attacker must lock 100 bonds, tying up capital for the full period even if the accounts earn nothing.
